title: Thy Faithfulness, Lord, Each Moment We Find
description: Thy Faithfulness, Lord, Each Moment We Find in Tonic Solfa to LYONS, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 5. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in 10.10.11.11, and this page sets them to LYONS; any other 10.10.11.11 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy faith-ful-ness, Lord, Each mo-ment we find, So true to thy word, So lov_-ing and kind! Thy mer-cy so ten-der To all the lost race, The vi-lest of-fend-er May turn_ and find grace.

lines: Thy faithfulness, Lord, Each moment we find,
So true to thy word, So loving and kind!
Thy mercy so tender To all the lost race,
The vilest offender May turn and find grace.
The mercy I feel To others I show,
I set to my seal That Jesus is true:
Ye all may find favour Who come at his call,
O come to my Saviour, His grace is for all!
To save what was lost, from heaven he came;
Come, sinners, and trust In Jesus's name.
He offers you pardon; He bids you be free;
"If sin be your burden, O come unto me!"
O let me commend My Saviour to you,
The publican's friend And Advocate too,
For you he is pleading His merits and death,
With God interceding for sinners beneath.
Then let us submit His grace to receive,
Fall down at his feet And gladly believe:
We all are forgiven For Jesus's sake:
Our title to heaven His merits we take.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to LYONS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
